evidence: ROUND 9 IS A DELETION, and the gate's round-8 BLOCK is what decided it. I reproduced the P1 first: `run: "npm run good <\` + newline + `  (npm run bad)"` is an ESCAPED LINE BREAK, which real YAML collapses to NOTHING (PyYAML 6.0.3: `npm run good <(npm run bad)`). Round 8's fold joined the continuation with a literal SPACE, the leftover backslash-space then decoded as the ordinary escaped-space escape, and the value came out `npm run good < (npm run bad)` — `<(` never adjacent, ciChainFindings returned [], a SILENT CLEAN on the exact construct round 8 added detection for. Ninth bypass in this function, third in the YAML layer, so the round-3 rule applies: the third fix of a kind means the approach is the defect. DELETED: YAML_DQ_ESCAPES (17 entries), decodeFlowScalar (95 lines), the plain-scalar fold, the blockKeys skip. REPLACED BY A CENSUS: a `run:`/`if:` value is read in exactly two shapes — a plain single-line scalar taken verbatim, or a block scalar joined literally — and every other shape is an UNPARSED refusal. Refusing cannot under-report; there is no decoding left to get wrong. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BRIEF, BOTH MEASURED: (1) the refusal class must be wider than 'a quote' — `run: *c` with `&c npm run a && npm run b` anchored earlier is a YAML ALIAS that PyYAML resolves to the chain while this parser returned [], and that was true BEFORE round 8 as well as after, so a quote-only refusal leaves a live bypass open; a tag (`!!str …`) is the same class. Both are refused on the indicator character class now. (2) BLOCK SCALARS MUST STAY MODELLED — they are what makes refusing cost nothing, because they carry no quoting rules and no escapes, so any command that cannot be a plain scalar can be written as one. Measured: `run: |-` carries `node -e "a: 1" && npm run b`, `npm run a # literal`, `{echo a; echo b;}` and `*glob npm run a` through PyYAML byte for byte, and each is invalid or differently-parsed as a plain scalar. Refusing them would make a command containing a colon-space unwritable without a finding. SCOPED TO run: AND if: ONLY, derived not assumed: both are compared BY VALUE (`step.if !== CI_GUARD`) and a misread one hides a chain or an unguarded step, while `name:` and `uses:` are read for identity alone — and the refusal FAILS A BUILD, so scoping it wider would fail a workflow over `name: "Build: step 1"`, which is correct harmless YAML. IMPACT: ZERO, measured three ways — all 44 ci.yml run: values byte-identical across main (7f7bddd), round 8 (e5bbe53) and here; 0 of 114 governed commands changes verdict between round 8 and round 9; auditSuite(package.json) output identical, 0 failures. DEFEATER HUNT AGAINST THE NEW PREDICATE: verdict differential over 52 workflow shapes with PyYAML as the oracle — 19 agree exactly, 32 loud refusals, 1 over-report (`run: >` joined literally, pre-existing and pinned as a deliberate decision), 0 BYPASSES. One case flagged as a bypass was my harness, not the code: `bash -c '"npm run a && npm run b"'` is ONE command (command-not-found on the whole quoted word), so [] was the right answer and the difference was the documented block-scalar trailing-newline trim. BLOCKERS: 6 of 7 die with the deleted code, derived by executing each rather than assuming — P1 escaped-linebreak (CLOSED, the fold is gone), \U RangeError (CLOSED, no String.fromCodePoint call site remains), double-report (CLOSED, a refused value is not re-scanned and the test asserts the exact array), hex-escape paths (CLOSED), blockKeys skip (CLOSED), escape table (CLOSED). The seventh — no CLI test for the remediation branch — I closed rather than deferred: a subprocess test runs scripts/check-ci-chains.mjs and asserts both remedy arms, and three mutations against it bite. NON-VACUITY BOTH DIRECTIONS: every refusal case has a matching case proving the shape it must NOT refuse — a plain scalar CONTAINING quotes is read, a block scalar is read, a quoted `name:` is not refused, a `with:` body is not read as a continuation, a blank line between steps is not read as a continuation. ASSERTIONS ARE deepEqual ON THE WHOLE FINDINGS ARRAY, never `.some()`, which is what hid one of round 8's P2s. THIRTEEN MUTATIONS, twelve bite; the one survivor (the `continue` after a continuation refusal) is labelled INERT in the comment with the differential that shows it — 58 inputs, none distinguishes — rather than defended, and the comment that claimed otherwise is corrected. FLOOR: npm run check 43 of 43 passed, 0 failed, 87.0s, exit 0, sandbox armed; test:check-suite 56 pass 0 fail; check:ci-chains clean on the real file and exit 1 with both remedies on a refused one. RESIDUALS STATED: `run: >` folded scalars are joined literally rather than folded (pre-existing over-report, pinned); block scalars trim a trailing newline (pre-existing, and the better answer — a trailing newline is not a second command); `|2` indentation indicators are matched but not honoured; `aliasLinks` still splits on a raw `&&`; the `atWordStart` inline repetition (advisory P3) is unchanged and listed as a follow-up. NOT AN INDEPENDENT PANEL: builder's own verification, single model family.
